notes.title: v1.3 Experimental Multiplayer Update
notes.content:
Multiplayer has been one of the most requested features since day one of the game's release. It's to be expected, multiplayer functionality is standard in games of this type. However, I avoided doing it for a couple reasons. One, I didn't know how. I still don't really know how, but using steam's built in p2p functionality I managed to cobble something together. Second, the game's code is a mess, and certain aspects of it are NOT built in a way that would allow multiplayer to work. This late in the game's production, it's an absolute mess to work with. I had standards, and I didn't want to make multiplayer when I knew it wasn't going to be fully functional. 

I put the project down with the last update, and decided to move on to other things.

The other day though I thought to myself: wouldn't BAD multiplayer be better than NO multiplayer? So I got to work, and this update is the result. I'm labeling it as "experimental" because the functionality is pretty poor and will be prone to issues. There's also missing features, enemies are not synced at all (this is because they use lots of rng and are also not built to handle multiple players. Implementing them would mean rewriting and changing the behavior of every enemy in the game, something I'm not willing to do.) 

You can build stuff together though, and I think that's enough for at least some people to have some fun with.

To create a lobby, open up a world or create a new one. Pause the game, and in the pause menu there will be an option to "create lobby". To join a lobby, press "lobbies" on the main menu. If your lobby is public, it will appear on this list. If not, you'll have to get the lobby id from the host, which you'll be able to see on the pause menu in game.



Changes:

New experimental multiplayer !

New lobby screen on the main menu

Ability to create lobbies in pause menu

Chat messages take longer to disappear

Command line is now "chat box"

Chat box will open when pressing "Enter" and in a multiplayer game

Running commands will now require you to type "/" before them. Not doing so will send a regular chat message

Chat messages are no longer framerate dependent

Added a new pair of pants to honor a certain corn stick mascot

notes.title: update v1.1.4
notes.content:
Technical changes:
	
 buffed flashlight trinket


Bug Fixes:
	
 options menu no longer starts scrolled down to the bottom
 	fixed bug where playing on higher fps could sometimes deal fall damage innapropriately
 	flashlight trinket now works while climbing ladders
 	shift clicking armor now properly updates it
 	fishing input delay now uses deltatime and should work on higher fps
 	fixed vsync text in the options not updating when booting up the game


v1.1.4 is just a small patch that fixes a couple bugs the discord has found since last update. I'm sure some of yall are wondering what the future of waxweaver will look like, so I wanted to talk about it a bit. Firstly, let me be clear: waxweaver is NOT going to get the same long term support as games like terraria or minecraft. I think a lot of people expect long term support because the industry staples of the genre do, and conceptually, yes a game like this could be updated forever. There are a few things I do want to add, but be aware that v1.2 might be the last update the game receives. I'm mostly saying all this, because I don't wanna accidentally drum up hype just to leave people disappointed later down the road. I wanted to make something fun, and I'm ready to move on to other projects and learn new things ( i'm trying to learn p2p stuff right now! ). Reminder that the game is open source on github and I encourage anyone whos interested to try making mods.

The updates I do have planned are pretty small, but should hopefully add a bit more depth to the game overall. Thanks for playin yall.
